fixes.explanation: Hold on, friend. A cloud that clocks in for one day and then quits? Not this one. The text says, “It remained that way continually…” It covered the tabernacle by day and looked like fire at night (Numbers 9:16). Day shift, night shift, no days off.

Reminder it is, baker! The trumpets are to be blown “…to serve as a reminder for you before your God.” The command covers joyous occasions, appointed feasts and the beginning of each month. That beats a sticky note on the fridge by a mile.

I get why warning came to mind, because a trumpet can sound like an alarm. But this verse is about joyous occasions, appointed feasts and the beginning of each month. That's party territory. The trumpets are to be blown “…to serve as a reminder for you before your God.” (Numbers 10:10)

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
“All got the sound” presents the trumpet instructions as events that happened. The passage gives the command but does not say it was carried out.
“Nobody hits snooze on a feast” blends an alarm-clock comparison with the feast and does not make a clear connection.
